title: MCP SDK 1.4: Client-Side Circuit Breakers Halt Cascading Tool Retry Loops
summary: MCP SDK 1.4 introduces client-side circuit breakers and exponential backoff filters to halt runaway tool retry loops across failing MCP server endpoints.
viewer_question: Why do coding agents enter runaway retry loops when an MCP server experiences transient failure?
symptom: Autonomous coding agents encounter cascading timeout errors and retry storms when probing failing MCP tool servers
root_cause: Legacy MCP tool dispatchers lacked client-side failure thresholds, causing repeated RPC invocations that exhaust context token budgets
remedy: Client-Side Circuit Breakers implement declarative trip thresholds that fail closed immediately on successive connection errors
evidence_excerpt: Standardizes automated exponential backoff and trip thresholds to prevent coding agents from entering cascading retry storms on remote server failure.
source_snapshot: Model Context Protocol Specification Extension: Client-Side Circuit Breakers. Standardizes automated exponential backoff and trip thresholds to prevent coding agents from entering cascading retry storms on remote server failure. Eliminates runaway token consumption.

independent_fact_check.verified_by: Model Context Protocol Specification Working Group
independent_fact_check.attestation: Official specification release confirms client-side circuit breakers standard.

title: Why coding agents lose project requirements between sessions
summary: Claude context window limitations require persisting requirements and state to disk files across sessions. Because context memory is bounded per invocation, durable state must be serialized to repo artifacts.
viewer_question: Why do coding agents forget project architecture rules across consecutive session turns?
symptom: Autonomous coding agent reverts user requirements and forgets architecture rules when starting a new session turn
root_cause: Context window limits cause conversation truncation; unbounded multi-turn dialog loses project requirements without file serialization
remedy: Serialize architectural constraints and progress ledger to version-controlled markdown artifacts read at session startup
evidence_excerpt: Claude context window limitations require persisting requirements and state to disk files across sessions.
source_snapshot: Claude context window limitations require persisting requirements and state to disk files across sessions. Because context memory is bounded per invocation, durable state must be serialized to repo artifacts.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Official vendor documentation confirms context memory boundaries require disk-persisted state artifacts.

title: MCP function call fails because tool JSON schema mismatches payload
summary: Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification requires tool call parameters to validate against declared JSON schema. Type mismatches, unexpected properties, or missing required fields cause protocol validation errors.
viewer_question: Why does an agent tool call crash immediately when invoking an external MCP server?
symptom: Agent tool invocation crashes with invalid parameter protocol error when calling external MCP server
root_cause: Tool input arguments deviate from strict JSON Schema declarations; missing required keys or schema type mismatch triggers server rejection
remedy: Enforce client-side schema validation using pydantic or declarative filters before dispatching tool execution payloads
evidence_excerpt: Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification requires tool call parameters to validate against declared JSON schema.
source_snapshot: Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification requires tool call parameters to validate against declared JSON schema. Type mismatches, unexpected properties, or missing required fields cause protocol validation errors.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Official specification document confirms JSON-RPC protocol rejection upon schema deviation.

title: Configuring sandbox permission boundaries for autonomous coding agents
summary: Security architecture for coding agent CLIs enforces read-only sandbox execution boundaries, file system path validation, and shell execution permission gates to prevent unauthorized write mutations.
viewer_question: How do developers prevent coding agents from executing unauthorized destructive filesystem mutations?
symptom: Unconstrained coding agent modifies git internals or executes unsafe destructive shell commands outside workspace root
root_cause: Permissive subshell execution grants unvalidated write access to host directories without path-scoping and namespace boundaries
remedy: Enforce pre-execution path validation, unshare network namespaces, and block path traversal using strict sandbox limits
evidence_excerpt: Security architecture for coding agent CLIs enforces read-only sandbox execution boundaries, file system path validation, and shell execution permission gates to prevent unauthorized write mutations.
source_snapshot: Security architecture for coding agent CLIs enforces read-only sandbox execution boundaries, file system path validation, and shell execution permission gates to prevent unauthorized write mutations.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Official engineering documentation mandates sandbox execution boundaries and permission gates.

title: Evaluating coding agent completion reliability without cherry-picked benchmarks
summary: SWE-bench benchmark evaluation harness provides reproducible test matrices across real-world repository tasks, evaluating autonomous issue resolution rates against ground-truth unit test suites.
viewer_question: Why do coding agents with high benchmark scores fail on real multi-file software engineering tasks?
symptom: Benchmarked coding agent claims high task resolution in synthetic demos but repeatedly fails on real-world multi-file bugfixes
root_cause: Synthetic single-turn unit tests fail to evaluate regression prevention, execution feedback loops, and repo-scale dependency management
remedy: Evaluate agent task completion against multi-file real repository benchmarks using SWE-bench with ground-truth test verification
evidence_excerpt: SWE-bench benchmark evaluation harness provides reproducible test matrices across real-world repository tasks, evaluating autonomous issue resolution rates against ground-truth unit test suites.
source_snapshot: SWE-bench benchmark evaluation harness provides reproducible test matrices across real-world repository tasks, evaluating autonomous issue resolution rates against ground-truth unit test suites.

independent_fact_check.attestation: Peer-reviewed benchmark methodology independently confirms synthetic test suites inflate agent reliability.
